what_happened: The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path moved right, but the ego slowly drifted left across the lane edge. At 8.9 s it went onto the grass median with palm trees, about 6.4 m from the recorded path. The metrics table counts no collision, only the offroad, and the camera view stayed clean until the ego was already on the median.

The ego was going straight at about 9.5 m/s toward an intersection, with car 33 driving alongside in the lane to its left. After the policy took over at 4.7 s, the ego drifted about 1.3 m left of the recorded path and sideswiped car 33 at 6.4 s; the lead car was 17 m ahead, so braking for it was not the issue.

After handoff, the ego sped up from about 8.5 to 9.3 m/s on a narrow residential street. It held a line along the left edge, left of both the recorded path and its own planned green line, then drifted into the left parking lane and clipped the rear right corner of parked car 31 with its front, which also counts as offroad.

The route turns right at the intersection, but the command showed STRAIGHT until 6.0 s. The policy's plan bent left toward the through lanes, and at 6.0 s, still around 4.5 m/s, the ego's box crossed the lane edge and was flagged offroad. It was only 0.5 m from the human's recorded path at that moment, so the offroad flag may come from a tight map boundary as much as from the policy's leftward drift, which had barely begun.

The ego reached the stop line at about 7 m/s, one second after the policy took over at 4.7 s. Its planned path (orange) swung hard left across the intersection even though the command had just changed to RIGHT, and the offroad flag fired while the ego was only 0.5 m from the recorded human path. A deviation that small suggests the human line runs along the edge of the mapped drivable area, so the flag may be partly a map-boundary artifact rather than a real departure.

After crossing the intersection heading north, the ego drifted left toward the left-side parking lane and hit parked car 68 (the dark Audi) with its front. It held about 4.5 m/s the whole time and never braked, even as the gap closed from 23 m to 4 m. The later rear contact came after this front collision.

As the ego crossed the intersection into a narrow street lined with parked cars, it ran about 1.5 m left of the recorded path at about 5 m/s. Its front-left corner clipped parked car 68 at the left curb at the street entrance. It wasn't a lead-vehicle or turning conflict: it was a lateral misjudgment that made the ego sideswipe a parked car.

After the policy took over at 4.6 s, the ego sped up from 8.6 to 9.4 m/s and drifted left, away from the route line, into the lane of cars parked on the left. At 6.8 s its front hit parked car 31. Its own planned path (orange) kept tracking left along the parked cars instead of staying in the travel lane, and the camera view before the crash is clear, so the policy is to blame. The rear contact recorded for the run is not what caused the failure.

The ego held about 9.5 m/s through the intersection approach and kept a 17 m gap to the car ahead, so this was not a rear-end. When the command changed to RIGHT, the ego's planned path bent right and the ego drifted 1.2 m off the recorded path. It then side-swiped an adjacent car, most likely car 33 just to its left; the frames don't clearly show which neighbor it hit.

The route command was RIGHT, but after handoff the policy kept steering the ego left, away from the recorded path (6 m off by the end). At 8.7 s it drove at about 9 m/s onto the landscaped median with palm trees on the left. No vehicle was involved: every collision metric reads 0 and the lead car stayed more than 24 m ahead.

The ego was approaching the intersection at about 4.5 m/s with a right turn on the route. After handoff at 4.7s, the policy's plan pointed straight/left, away from the right turn, and at 6.0s the offroad flag fired. The ego was only 0.5 m from where the human drove, though, and in the map it still looks inside the lane, so this may be a map or metric quirk at the intersection mouth rather than a real departure.

The command was RIGHT and the recorded human path moved right toward the turn. Instead, the policy slowly drifted left across its lane and steered into the landscaped median, where it went off the road at 8.8 s, about 6 m from the human path. The camera view was clean until the ego was already on the median, and no other actor was involved in the departure.

The command was RIGHT, but at the intersection the ego crept straight ahead and drifted left of its planned route (3.3 m off the recorded path) into the crossing path of car 112, which was moving through the intersection toward the ego's front-left. The ego only slowed from 2.6 to 1.9 m/s as the gap closed from 26 m to 4 m, and its front hit 112.

The command was RIGHT and the route turned right, but after handoff the ego planned a path to the left. It stayed at about 10 m/s, drifted left away from the route (6.2 m off the recording at the failure) and drove over the curb into the tree-lined median at 8.9 s. No other actor was involved, and the camera view was clean until the ego was already in the median.

Even though the route said RIGHT and the recorded path curved right, the ego drifted left out of its lane and drove onto the grass median at about 9 m/s. At 9.0 s it was among the palm trees, 6.3 m from where the human drove. The camera view was clean before the failure, so it doesn't explain the drift.

Despite a RIGHT command, the ego drove straight through the intersection at a steady ~4.6 m/s. Its planned path then curved left toward the row of parked cars, and it hit parked car 68 with its front-left at 8.2 s without braking. The rear contact recorded in the run came after this front collision.

The road ahead was clear, but after the policy took over at 4.6 s the ego sped up (8.5 to 9.3 m/s) and its planned path (orange) kept bending left, away from the recorded human path on the right. The ego drifted into the left parking lane and its front hit parked car 31 at 6.7 s.

After handoff at 4.7 s, the ego was driving at about 9.5 m/s toward an intersection with a STRAIGHT command, which changed to RIGHT at the end. Its planned path (orange) bent left, away from the recorded route (green), and it drifted into the left lane, where its front hit actor 33 alongside at 6.4 s.

Approaching the intersection at about 4.5 m/s on a route that turns right, the policy planned to go straight/slightly left instead of following the right-turn route, and the ego edged left. About 1.3 s after handoff it was flagged offroad at the stop line, only 0.5–0.6 m from the recorded human path. No collision occurred and the gap to the lead car was over 30 m.

The command was RIGHT and the recorded path curved right, but after handoff the policy steered left across the double yellow centerline into the oncoming lane at about 11 m/s. It hit oncoming vehicle 85 head-on: the gap closed from 30.6 m to 3.6 m in 0.5 s, which is much faster than the ego alone could close it. At impact the ego was 9 m off the recorded trajectory.

The ego was going straight at a steady ~8.3 m/s with vehicle 33 driving alongside in the lane to its left. After handoff, the ego yawed left (the map rotates and the ego ends up ~1.2 m left of the recorded path) and its front-left side swiped vehicle 33, even though the route was about to turn right. The gap to the lead car stayed ~20 m, so braking for a car ahead was not the issue.

The route command was RIGHT and the route line went to the right lanes. Instead, the ego kept going at about 7 m/s in the leftmost turn-pocket lane, and its own plan (orange line) curved further left. It drove up onto the palm-tree median and went offroad at 9.7 s, 6.4 m from the recorded human path. There was no actor nearby, and the camera view was clean until the ego was already on the median.

With a RIGHT command, the ego drifted left of the recorded path, 4–8 m off by 7.3–8.3 s. Its planned path then curved left across the curb onto the corner sidewalk toward a parking lot, and it left the road at 9.3 s at about 4.6 m/s, 12 m from the human trajectory. The camera was somewhat smeared because the ego was off the recorded path, but the curb and sidewalk were still clearly visible, so the policy steered off the road on its own.

After the 4.7 s handoff the ego kept going about 9.5 m/s and its planned path (orange) drifted left, toward the lane where actor 33 was driving right beside it. At 6.4 s the ego's side hit actor 33. The car ahead was still about 17 m away, and the route command had just switched to RIGHT.
